title: Comparing the Dynamic Charge Response Measured with Transmission- and Reflection EELS
content: Quantum many body systems in condensed matter represent a treasure trove of unexplored- and poorly understood physics. The interplay between charge, spin, and structure gives rise to diverse competing electronic phases [1–3]. In order to further advance our understanding of such systems, one needs to study their collective response. The collective response is quantized by the dynamic charge response χ(q,ω). As the low-energy dynamics are inherently delocalized in nature, high momentum- as well as energy resolution is necessary to measure the quantity accurately [4]. Recent advances in the development of monochromated aberration-corrected (scanning) transmission electron microscopy (MAC-STEM) now enable probing excitations on the meV-scale.
